title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benviplot provides color palettes ggplot2 helper functions exploratory data analysis. color schemes based Benvi, brand Brazilian proptech QuintoAndar.1 package includes custom ggplot2 theme, discrete continuous color scales, wrappers common chart types.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
code: # Install remotes if needed install.packages("remotes")  remotes::install_github("viniciusoike/benviplot")

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benviplot bundles Poppins font family. systemfonts ragg available, package registers Poppins theme_benvi() uses default. Otherwise, theme uses system sans-serif font. Install ragg render Poppins PNG files. Base PDF PostScript devices use fonts registered systemfonts; use base_family = "sans" devices. Check whether Poppins ragg available font_status().
code: install.packages("ragg") font_status()

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: Combine theme_benvi() scale_*_benvi_*() functions style ggplot2 chart. example , scale_fill_benvi_d() maps discrete cylinder variable "qual_8" qualitative palette. theme_benvi() sets remaining theme elements.
code: library(ggplot2) library(benviplot) ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, fill = as.factor(cyl))) +   geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, color = "#000000") +   scale_fill_benvi_d(name = "Cylinders", pal_name = "qual_8") +   labs(     title = "Fuel Efficiency vs. Weight",     x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",     y = "Miles per Gallon"   ) +   theme_benvi()

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: package organizes palettes theme, sequential, qualitative, diverging, city-specific, brand families. Choose family based variable role color chart.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: show_palettes() displays available palettes. Calling without arguments shows every palette; pass type name narrow output. Filter display "theme", "sequential", "qualitative", "diverging", "city", "brand".
code: show_palettes() show_palettes("sequential")

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benvi_palette() returns palette object backed hexadecimal color values. Printing object draws color swatches active graphics device.  pass colors another package, coerce result plain character vector. Discrete palettes contain 4 9 fixed colors. Set type = "continuous" interpolate colors along palette gradient.
code: # Preview a palette benvi_palette("qual_2") # Get hex codes as a plain character vector as.character(benvi_palette("benvi_blue")) #>  [1] "#021841" "#192C50" "#2F405F" "#46546E" "#5D687D" "#737C8C" "#8A919C" #>  [8] "#A0A5AB" "#B7B9BA" "#CECDC9" benvi_palette("seq_greens", n = 20, type = "continuous")

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: scale functions follow ggplot2 naming pattern scale_{aesthetic}_benvi_{d|c}(). suffix d denotes discrete scale, c denotes continuous scale. color fill variants available; colour spellings aliases color functions.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: Discrete scales map categorical variables fixed colors. Qualitative palettes usually work best purpose, pal_name accepts package palette.
code: iqaiw_total <- subset(iqaiw, rooms == "Total")  ggplot(iqaiw_total, aes(x = date, y = index, color = name_muni)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 100) +   scale_color_benvi_d("rio_qual", name = NULL) +   labs(     title = "IQAIW Rental Index by City",     x = NULL,     y = "Index (base = 100)"   ) +   theme_benvi()

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: Continuous scales interpolate colors package palette. Sequential palettes usually work best ordered numeric values. Use direction = -1 reverse palette.
code: iqaiw_total <- subset(iqaiw_total, !is.na(acum12m))  ggplot(iqaiw_total, aes(x = date, y = name_muni, fill = acum12m * 100)) +   geom_tile(height = 0.6, color = "#ffffff") +   scale_fill_benvi_c(     pal_name = "benvi_blue",     name = "YoY Change (%)",     direction = -1   ) +   scale_x_date(     date_breaks = "1 year",     date_labels = "%Y",     expand = expansion(0)   ) +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +   theme_benvi() +   theme(     legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.75),     axis.text = element_text(size = 12),     panel.grid = element_blank()   )

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: benviplot includes wrappers common chart types. functions accept data frame unquoted column names, apply theme_benvi(), return ggplot object. Build charts directly ggplot2 need finer control.

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_line() draws single-series line chart. Pass color map grouping variable draw multiple lines legend.
code: spo_index <- subset(iqaiw, name_muni == "São Paulo" & rooms == "Total") plot_line(spo_index, x = date, y = index)

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_column() creates vertical bar chart. Setting text = TRUE adds value labels bar. Set text_inside = TRUE place labels inside bars; option requires ggfittext package.
code: latest_sales <- subset(   sales_report,   name_muni == "Belo Horizonte" & date == max(date) )  plot_column(latest_sales, x = name_zone, y = price_m2, text = TRUE)

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_scatter() maps x y scatter plot. Pass variable color apply Benvi palette points. Set fit = TRUE add fitted line.
code: plot_scatter(   mtcars,   x = wt,   y = mpg,   color = as.factor(cyl),   pal_name = "qual_5",   scale_name = "Cylinders",   fit = TRUE )

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_area() draws single area maps grouping variable fill draw stacked areas.
code: room_index <- subset(   iqaiw,   name_muni == "São Paulo" & rooms %in% c("1", "2", "3") )  plot_area(room_index, x = date, y = index, fill = rooms)

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: plot_histogram() selects bin width Freedman–Diaconis rule default. Set bins choose number bins directly.
code: plot_histogram(mtcars, x = mpg)

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: helpers return ggplot objects, can add layers, scales, theme adjustments usual ggplot2 syntax.
code: plot_line(spo_index, x = date, y = index) +   geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = benvi_palette("oranges")[3]) +   labs(     title = "Rental Price Index in São Paulo",     subtitle = "Smoothed trend",     x = NULL,     y = "Index (base = 100)",     caption = "Source: IQAIW"   )

title: Getting Started with benviplot
text: palettes tied ggplot2. Convert palette character vector use hexadecimal color values base R graphics, lattice, another plotting system.
code: colors <- as.character(benvi_palette("purples"))  plot(   mtcars$wt,   mtcars$mpg,   col = colors[mtcars$cyl / 2 - 1],   pch = 19,   cex = 1.5,   xlab = "Weight (1000 lbs)",   ylab = "Miles per Gallon",   main = "Using Benvi colors in base R" )

title: Getting Started with benviplot

title: benviplot • Color Palettes for Data Visualization
text: Use one following scale functions apply palettes plot. scale_color_benvi_d() scale_color_benvi_c() scale_fill_benvi_c() scale_fill_benvi_d() Use theme_benvi() apply package theme.  using continuous scale colors interpolated.  plot_*() helpers create common charts exploratory analysis. example, plot_column(text = TRUE) adds value labels columns.  examples, visit package website.
code: # Rental price index for major cities index_data <- iqaiw |>   filter(     rooms %in% c("1", "2"),     between(date, as.Date("2023-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-31"))   )  ggplot(index_data, aes(date, index, color = rooms)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +   facet_wrap(vars(name_muni)) +   scale_color_benvi_d() +   labs(     title = "IQAIW Rental Index by City",     x = NULL,     y = "Index (base = 100)",     color = "Rooms",     caption = "Source: IQAIW (benviplot)"   ) +   theme_benvi() # Year-over-year change by city over time index_data <- iqaiw |>   filter(     rooms == "Total",     between(date, as.Date("2023-01-01"), as.Date("2025-12-31"))   )  ggplot(index_data, aes(x = date, y = name_muni, fill = acum12m * 100)) +   geom_tile(height = 0.6, color = "gray90") +   scale_fill_benvi_c(     pal_name = "benvi_blue",     name = "YoY Change (%)",     direction = -1   ) +   scale_x_date(     date_breaks = "1 year",     date_labels = "%Y",     expand = expansion(0)   ) +   labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +   theme_benvi() +   theme(     legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.75),     axis.text = element_text(size = 12),     panel.grid = element_blank()   ) latest_sales <- subset(   sales_report,   name_muni == "Belo Horizonte" & date == max(date) )  plot_column(latest_sales, x = name_zone, y = price_m2, text = TRUE)

title: Format numbers using Brazilian conventions — format_num_br
text: Brazilian number formatting uses . thousands separator , decimal separator. example, 1234567.89 becomes "1.234.567,9" digits = 1.

title: Format numbers using Brazilian conventions — format_num_br
code: # Basic formatting x <- 1235134.123 format_num_br(x) #> [1] "1.235.134"  # Different decimal places format_num_br(x, digits = 3) #> [1] "1.235.134" format_num_br(x, digits = 0) #> [1] "1.235.134"  # With percentage format_num_br(12.5, digits = 1, percent = TRUE) #> [1] "12,5%"  # Negative digits round to tens, hundreds, etc. format_num_br(1234567, digits = -3) #> [1] "1.235.000"  # Works with vectors format_num_br(c(100, 1000, 10000)) #> [1] "100"    "1.000"  "10.000"

what: Save a ggplot with benviplot defaults — ggsave_benvi
title: Save a ggplot with benviplot defaults — ggsave_benvi
text: wrapper around ggplot2::ggsave() uses ragg graphics device PNG output. Registered fonts bundled Poppins visible systemfonts-aware devices, ragg lets theme_benvi() render font saved files. ragg installed, function uses default graphics device.

title: Save a ggplot with benviplot defaults — ggsave_benvi
code: ggsave_benvi(   filename,   plot = ggplot2::last_plot(),   device = NULL,   width = 7,   height = 5,   units = "in",   dpi = 300,   ... )

title: Save a ggplot with benviplot defaults — ggsave_benvi
text: filename File name create disk. file extension determines graphics device (example, ".png", ".pdf", ".svg"). plot Plot save. Defaults last plot displayed. device Graphics device. Uses ragg::agg_png() PNG files ragg installed. Otherwise, uses ggplot2's default device. width, height Plot size. Defaults 7 5 inches. units Units width height. Choose "", "cm", "mm", "px". Defaults "". dpi DPI use raster graphics. Defaults 300. ... Additional arguments passed ggplot2::ggsave().

title: Save a ggplot with benviplot defaults — ggsave_benvi
text: filename, invisibly.

title: Save a ggplot with benviplot defaults — ggsave_benvi
code: p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point() ggsave_benvi(tempfile(fileext = ".png"), plot = p) #> ✔ Using ragg device for high-quality PNG output

title: Plot a histogram chart — plot_histogram
text: method parameter controls function computes bin width. "fd" "FD" Freedman-Diaconis rule. Uses interquartile range: \(2 * IQR / n^{1/3}\). "Scott" Scott's rule. formula uses standard deviation, \(3 * sd / n^{1/3}\). "Sturges" Sturges' formula. Uses \(k = \lceil log_2(n) \rceil\) bins. "Rice" Rice rule. Uses \(k = \lceil 2n^{1/3} \rceil\) bins. "sqrt" Square-root rule. Uses \(k = \lceil \sqrt{n} \rceil\) bins.

title: Plot a histogram chart — plot_histogram
